questions.question: What's your DevTools workflow for debugging rendering, JS, and network issues — the panels and the advanced tricks?
questions.title: Devtools Workflow
questions.direct_answer: The panel-per-problem map: Elements (DOM + styles — the Computed pane for RESOLVED values, Cascade for WHY a rule lost, the 'struck-through loser' story; force element states :hover/:focus for unreachable states) · Console (the command-line API: $0 = selected element, getEventListeners, monitorEvents, copy) · Sources (breakpoints incl. CONDITIONAL, the Async stack checkbox for promise chains, scope/watch live bindings, blackboxing libraries) · Network (waterfall: DNS/TCP/TLS/TTFB breakdown, throttling profiles, the Initiator column — WHO triggered the request; blocked/queued stalls vs slow responses) · Performance (record + read the long-task breakdown — scripting/layout/paint — the jank diagnosis) · Memory/Application (heap snapshots' detached-DOM leak hunt, storage inspectors). The power-user layer: workspaces (persist DevTools edits to disk), local overrides (mock API responses without a proxy), and the Rendering panel (paint flashing, layout shift regions, LCP markers).

sections.title: Interview Answer
sections.content:
The map, as workflow commands:

```text
PROBLEM                        → PANEL + MOVE
'wrong style applies'         → Elements → Computed (resolved value)
                                 → Cascade pane (read the struck-through
                                   loser + its specificity/origin)
'handler doesn't fire'        → Elements → Event Listeners pane;
                                 console: getEventListeners($0)
'where did this throw?'       → Sources → breakpoint + 'Async' stack
                                 checkbox (connects await chains);
                                 CONDITIONAL bp stops only when x === undefined
'request slow / failing'     → Network → click the row: Timing waterfall
                                 (DNS/TCP/TLS/TTFB/content download);
                                 Initiator column = WHO fired it;
                                 throttle profile (Slow 4G) to reproduce
'page janky'                  → Performance → record the scroll, read
                                 long tasks >50ms: scripting vs layout vs paint
'memory grows'                → Memory → heap snapshot A, act, snapshot B,
                                 comparison view → 'Detached' nodes = leak
'mock the API'                → Sources → Overrides (or Network override):
                                 serve YOUR response file — no proxy needed
'repaint storms'             → Rendering panel → Paint flashing,
                                 Layout Shift regions, LCP marker
```

The console power tools (the ones that replace dozens of logs): $0 = the currently selected Elements node (Elements ⇄ Console ping-pong — select, then script against it); $(selector)/$$(selector) = the query shortcuts; getEventListeners($0) = the hidden listener inspection; monitorEvents($0, 'key') = live event stream; copy(obj) = clipboard for API payloads; console.table for array-of-objects; console.trace() for 'who called this'.

The workflow discipline (the interview differentiator): DevTools-first means EVIDENCE before hypothesis — the tool shows the ACTUAL computed value, the ACTUAL winning rule, the ACTUAL timing waterfall, the ACTUAL retained heap. The console.log instinct is a scalar; the panels are a microscope. Say the sequence: reproduce → pick the panel by symptom → read the evidence → form ONE hypothesis → verify → fix → prove with the same tool (and record the regression case).

sections.title: Mental Model
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    BUG{symptom class} -->|style| E[Elements: Computed + Cascade panes]
    BUG -->|js error| S[Sources: conditional bp + async stacks + scope]
    BUG -->|network| N[Network: Timing waterfall + Initiator + throttle]
    BUG -->|jank| P[Performance: long tasks breakdown]
    BUG -->|memory| M[Heap snapshots comparison + Detached nodes]
    BUG -->|requests mock| O[Overrides — replace API responses]
    C[Console CLI: $0, getEventListeners, monitorEvents, copy] --> LOG[replace log-sprinkling]
    EV[evidence before hypothesis] --> V[verify one hypothesis, fix, prove]
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
The breakpoint taxonomy (beyond the basic click): LINE breakpoints (the classic); CONDITIONAL (stop only when qty === undefined — no log spam on hot paths); DOM change breakpoints (subtree modifications, attribute changes — the 'who moved my element' debugger); XHR/fetch breakpoints (break on a URL substring — the request origin trace without the Initiator hunt); and event-listener breakpoints (break on ANY click handler — when you don't know which one fires). Blackboxing (Ignore List) steps through YOUR code, not libraries — the difference between debugging and drowning.

The Network waterfall semantics (the performance-consultancy layer): each row's Timing shows queueing → DNS → TCP → TLS → waiting/TTFB (server time — the backend's problem) → content download (network — the payload's problem). A long TTFB across all endpoints is the server; a long download on one asset is its size; stalled/queued parallel groups reveal the 6-connection HTTP/1.1 ceiling (HTTP/2 multiplexing solves — visible in the protocol column). The 'Disable cache' toggle while DevTools open (the one setting everyone should confirm — the #1 'my change didn't ship' false alarm), and 'Block request URL' (the failure-injection tool: test the app against a dead dependency — the error-path testing no one does in production code).

The memory-leak method (the one that needs procedure): snapshot A → perform the suspected leak action N times → snapshot B → comparison mode → look for growing objects, 'Detached' DOM trees (nodes removed from the document but retained by a listener — the classic), and closures retaining large scopes. The Allocation instrumentation-on-timeline records every allocation with stack traces — the surgical answer when comparison shows growth but not the culprit. The discipline: distinguish LIVE growth (a leak — fix the retention) from heap spikes (GC hasn't run — force a GC in the panel before concluding).
